question: How do you define SQLAlchemy models and what is the difference between the declarative and core approaches?
title: SQLAlchemy Declarative Models
direct_answer: Declarative (recommended): define Python classes inheriting from Base (DeclarativeBase in SQLAlchemy 2.0). Class attributes using Mapped[] type annotations define columns. The ORM maps Python objects to SQL rows. SQLAlchemy Core: work directly with Table objects and SQL constructs — lower-level, more control. Use Declarative for application code. Use Core for complex bulk operations where ORM overhead matters.
interviewer_intent: Tests SQLAlchemy 2.0 knowledge — many codebases still use 1.4 style, knowing the 2.0 declarative syntax signals up-to-date knowledge.

sections.title: SQLAlchemy 2.0 declarative models
sections.content:
SQLAlchemy 2.0 introduced typed declarative mappings using Python type annotations with Mapped[]. This replaces Column() with annotation-first syntax and makes type checkers work without plugins.

DeclarativeBase: the base class for all models. Primary keys: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True). Optional columns: Mapped[Optional[str]]. Server defaults: mapped_column(server_default=text('now()')). Relationships: relationship('Child', back_populates='parent').

sections.title: SQLAlchemy 2.0 model definition
sections.content:
from sqlalchemy import String, Text, ForeignKey, func
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, relationship
from sqlalchemy.types import DateTime
from typing import Optional
from datetime import datetime

class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    email: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(255), unique=True, index=True)
    username: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(50), unique=True)
    bio: Mapped[Optional[str]] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(default=True)
    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
        DateTime(timezone=True),
        server_default=func.now()
    )
    posts: Mapped[list['Post']] = relationship(back_populates='author', lazy='selectin')

class Post(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'posts'

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(200))
    body: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text)
    author_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey('users.id'))
    author: Mapped['User'] = relationship(back_populates='posts')

seo.metaDescription: SQLAlchemy 2.0 declarative models with Mapped[] type annotations, mapped_column, ForeignKey relationships, and lazy vs eager loading.

speakable_v2.hook: SQLAlchemy 2.0's Mapped[] annotations make your model definitions type-safe and work with mypy without plugins.

beats.content: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True) — the type annotation declares the Python type, mapped_column provides the column configuration. Optional columns: Mapped[Optional[str]].

relationship() declares the ORM-level link. back_populates keeps both sides in sync. lazy='selectin' is usually the right default for async code — loads related objects in a second query, not N queries.

speakable_v2.cap: SQLAlchemy 1.4 style (Column(), Integer) still works but Mapped[] is the 2.0 idiomatic way and what you should write in new code.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with relationship loading strategies — selectin vs joined vs lazy.
